headline: US Dept of Energy Launches Genesis Open Models Initiative for Science
summary: The Genesis Mission aims to provide open-weight AI models to accelerate scientific discovery, with Arcee AI as the first industry partner. Applications for contributions close August 14, 2026.
details: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative, a new class of open-weight foundation models designed to accelerate scientific discovery. This initiative, part of the broader Genesis Mission, aims to provide researchers and the scientific community with transparent and adaptable AI models for various scientific domains.

Arcee AI is the first industry partner supporting this open-weights program. The first model in this class will be Genesis-Science-1, developed in collaboration with Arcee. The DOE seeks to foster shared infrastructure for science, enabling new workflows in fields like materials discovery, energy systems, and biology.

A contribution portal has been opened at genesisopenmodels.anl.gov for universities, national laboratories, companies, and research organizations interested in participating. Contributions can include data, research environments, evaluations, and technical expertise. The first round of applications is due August 14, 2026.

The initiative is grounded in the principles of open science, reproducibility, and responsible AI, with the goal of lowering barriers to advanced AI capabilities for public good. Selected contributors will work with DOE researchers, receive early access, and be credited in technical reports and release materials.
caption:
The US Department of Energy is launching a new initiative to accelerate scientific discovery with open-weight AI models. Applications for contributions are now open.

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative, a new class of open-weight foundation models designed to accelerate scientific discovery. This initiative, part of the broader Genesis Mission, aims to provide researchers and the scientific community with transparent and adaptable AI models for various scientific domains.

Arcee AI is the first industry partner supporting this open-weights program. The first model in this class will be Genesis-Science-1, developed in collaboration with Arcee. The DOE seeks to foster shared infrastructure for science, enabling new workflows in fields like materials discovery, energy systems, and biology.

A contribution portal has been opened at genesisopenmodels.anl.gov for universities, national laboratories, companies, and research organizations interested in participating. Contributions can include data, research environments, evaluations, and technical expertise. The first round of applications is due August 14, 2026.

The initiative is grounded in the principles of open science, reproducibility, and responsible AI, with the goal of lowering barriers to advanced AI capabilities for public good. Selected contributors will work with DOE researchers, receive early access, and be credited in technical reports and release materials.
